name: Alita-G: Self-Evolving Generative Agent for Agent Generation
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2510.23601, cs.AI), submitted 27 Oct 2025; 15 pages, 3 figures. No peer-reviewed venue as of mid-2026 [uncertain].
authors_affiliation: Jiahao Qiu, Xuan Qi, Hongru Wang (equal contribution); Xinzhe Juan, Yimin Wang, Zelin Zhao, Jiayi Geng, Jiacheng Guo, Peihang Li, Jingzhe Shi, Shilong Liu (corresponding), Mengdi Wang (corresponding). Affiliations: 1 Princeton University, 2 Tsinghua University, 3 The Chinese University of Hong Kong, 4 Shanghai Jiao Tong University, 5 University of Michigan, 6 King's College London, 7 Hong Kong University. Lead/PI lab: Mengdi Wang (Princeton).
code_url: No dedicated Alita-G code link is provided in the arXiv abstract or paper body. The framework builds directly on the open-sourced Alita generalist agent (https://github.com/CharlesQ9/Alita), which Alita-G extends; a standalone Alita-G repository is not cited in the paper. [uncertain]
task_domain: LLM-agent tool-use / deep-research and complex multi-step reasoning (general AI assistant tasks, medical visual QA, and frontier academic reasoning). Framed as automatic agent generation: turning a generalist tool-using agent into a domain-specialist agent.
problem_setting: Interactive, multi-component single-agent system (a Manager Agent plus a Web Agent, following the Alita framework). The setting has two phases. (1) An offline-style construction/self-evolution phase: a powerful generalist 'master' agent repeatedly executes a curated suite of target-domain tasks T={(x_i,y_i)} (each task run K times), and from SUCCESSFUL trajectories (where the master's answer matches the gold label) it synthesizes candidate MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools, which are abstracted into parameterized primitives and consolidated into an 'MCP Box'. Supervision here = task labels used only to filter successful runs (no gradient training of the LLM). (2) A test-time inference phase: given a new query, the specialized agent does retrieval-augmented MCP selection from the frozen MCP Box (cosine similarity over embeddings of MCP description+use_case vs. the query), then runs a CodeAct loop with an MCP Executor. The objective is that the specialized policy outperforms the base agent on the target task distribution while reducing compute (tokens).
what_is_retrieved: Tools/skills: parameterized, abstracted MCP tools (executable code modules with FastMCP-standardized interfaces plus a description and a use_case), synthesized from the master agent's successful task trajectories. Effectively reusable procedural skills/tools harvested from past successful experiences.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID-leaning toward a GROWING/induced memory: the retrievable store (MCP Box) is not a static external API corpus but is INDUCED offline by the agent itself from its own successful trajectories on the target task suite. After construction it is frozen for inference (no online growth at deployment), so within a single specialized-agent deployment it behaves like a fixed induced store; across construction iterations it grows. Closest to a self-built experiential tool memory rather than a static docs/KB corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Precision-driven variable-size selection (default) with an optional fixed top-k mode. The main/default setting uses threshold-based selection (keep all MCPs with cosine similarity >= tau=0.7), which yields a variable number of tools adapted to task complexity; an alternative top-k mode returns a fixed k. The paper argues threshold selection beats fixed top-k because different tasks need different numbers of MCPs. Not framed as a completeness/minimal-set recovery objective nor as a fixed top-k ranking objective; it is a relevance-threshold-driven variable-size recommendation.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve: yes (RAG MCP selection at inference). Reuse: yes (MCP Executor invokes selected tools). Revise/adapt: partial-no (no per-case revision of a retrieved tool at inference; abstraction/refinement happens once at construction). Retain: yes-but-offline (successful trajectories' MCPs are abstracted and retained into the MCP Box during construction, not during deployment). [Retrieve, Reuse, partial-Revise(construction-time abstraction only), Retain(offline)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It frames the work as MCP abstraction + MCP-level retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for self-evolution / automatic agent generation, though it realizes Retrieve/Reuse/Retain mechanisms that resemble CBR over tools rather than over cases.
retrieval_unit: tool-API / skill-or-program: a single abstracted MCP tool = {code, description, use_case}, i.e., a parameterized executable primitive distilled from a successful (sub-)trajectory. The retrieval granularity is one MCP tool per item.
index_source: Growing memory induced at construction time (not test-time): the store is built offline by running the master agent K times over the target task suite and harvesting MCPs from successful executions, then abstracting/refining them into the MCP Box. It is hybrid in that it requires a curated target task collection as the seed, but the retrievable items themselves are agent-self-generated rather than a pre-existing external corpus. Frozen during inference.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index keyed by a composite text representation (description concatenated with use_case), embedded with text-embedding-3-large and L2-normalized; retrieval is by cosine similarity over this flat set. The paper additionally builds an undirected similarity GRAPH (edges between MCP pairs with sim >= 0.7) purely as an ANALYSIS proxy for redundancy/clusters, not as the retrieval index. No hierarchical category->tool or dependency graph is used for selection.
retriever_type: Dense (off-the-shelf): semantic embedding retriever using a pre-trained text embedding model (OpenAI text-embedding-3-large by default) with cosine-similarity matching between the query embedding and each MCP's description+use_case embedding. No BM25, no learned/fine-tuned retriever, no generative tool-as-token retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf embedding model; no retriever training). The embedding encoder is frozen and pre-trained; selection is fixed cosine-similarity thresholding/top-k. The only 'learning'-like signal in the pipeline is downstream-task-effectiveness used as a FILTER during MCP construction (MCPs are kept only from successful trajectories), but that gates the index contents, not a trained retrieval policy.
query_construction: Raw new task query x_new is embedded directly with the embedding model phi to form e_query; no decomposition, no synthetic query expansion, no intent-extraction step is described. The MCP side key is the concatenation context_m = description_m (+) use_case_m.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single query embedding is computed for the incoming task and used to filter the MCP Box once before the CodeAct execution loop begins; selection is not re-issued per reasoning step.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: RAG-based MCP selection is performed a single time at the start of inference (the filtered MCP subset B_filtered is fixed before the while-loop), then the agent reasons/acts and invokes the already-selected MCPs as needed during the CodeAct loop. Not iterative/active/learned-router retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval/selection is triggered once at task initialization (deterministically, before reasoning begins) using the similarity threshold tau (or top-k). Within the loop, tool INVOCATION is agent-initiated (the reasoning engine decides when a tool is required and which MCP to call from the pre-filtered set), but no new RETRIEVAL from the full box is triggered mid-loop; there is no confidence/uncertainty/reflection-token retrieval trigger.
reranking: None. After cosine-similarity scoring, MCPs are filtered by threshold tau>=0.7 (or top-k) directly; no second-stage cross-encoder, hierarchy-aware, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker is applied.
retrieved_context_refinement: Rerank/none at retrieval time: only similarity thresholding (or top-k truncation) is applied to produce the focused tool subset; no decompose-then-recompose, reason-in-documents distillation, distractor filtering, or compression of the retrieved tools. (Refinement/abstraction of tool content is done earlier, at MCP Box construction, not post-retrieval.)
tool_document_engineering: Yes, substantial: during MCP abstraction each tool's documentation is engineered before indexing via (i) Parameter Generalization (hard-coded values -> configurable parameters), (ii) Context Removal (strip task-specific references), (iii) Interface Standardization (FastMCP-compatible interfaces), and (iv) Documentation Enhancement (comprehensive docstrings + type annotations). The retrievable text per MCP is the engineered description concatenated with the originating use_case; an ablation shows description+use_case > description-only > use_case-only for retrieval (83.03% vs 81.82% vs 77.57% on GAIA).
index_content_separation: Yes (lightweight index vs heavy content): retrieval is over a lightweight composite text (description (+) use_case) embedding, while the heavy executable MCP code is loaded/invoked on demand only after selection by the MCP Executor. This separates a cheap retrievable index from the on-demand tool code, and is explicitly motivated as mitigating prompt bloat / reducing tokens (~15% token savings).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Integration protocol: MCP (Model Context Protocol), specifically the FastMCP implementation, with a CodeAct loop and an MCP Executor for dynamic tool invocation; tools are standardized to FastMCP interfaces. The index itself is STATIC at inference (frozen MCP Box, no live CRUD auto-sync during deployment); it is updated only by re-running the offline construction with more iterations.
tool_dependency_awareness: No explicit inter-tool dependency modeling for retrieval. The paper notes the master agent is prompted to modularize sub-tasks into self-contained, standalone callable MCPs, and abstraction performs Context Removal to make each tool independent; the similarity graph used in analysis links near-duplicate (redundant) MCPs, not functional dependencies. No dependency graph / bipartite KG / dependency-aware reranking is used. [uncertain]
how_retrieved_used: Skill/tool reuse via prompt-augmented tool provisioning: the filtered, relevant MCP subset is supplied to the specialized agent, which runs a CodeAct loop; when the ReasoningEngine decides a tool is required it selects an MCP from the filtered set and the MCP Executor runs it, feeding the result back into context. Retrieval thus provisions a focused executable toolset rather than injecting demonstrations or training signal.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan/act: a one-shot RAG selection fixes a focused MCP toolset at task start, then a Manager Agent (with Task Analyzer, MCP Retriever, MCP Executor) runs an iterative CodeAct reason-act-observe loop that invokes the pre-selected MCPs. No tree search/MCTS; planning is the agent's standard interleaved reasoning-and-tool-use loop over a retrieval-narrowed action space.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call within a single rollout for tool USAGE (MCPs invoked as needed across CodeAct steps), but retrieval/selection from the box is per-answer (once per task at t=0). So: retrieval = per-answer; tool invocation = per-tool-call within the reasoning loop.
adaptation_mechanism: Construction-time LLM-prompted abstraction rather than per-case revision: a high-capacity LLM (LLM_abstract) transforms each raw, instance-specific MCP into a generalized parameterized primitive (parameter generalization, context removal, interface standardization, doc enhancement). At inference the retrieved MCP is reused largely as-is (parameters bound at call time by the agent); there is no execution-feedback-driven or critic-guided revision of the retrieved tool itself during deployment.
retrieved_item_representation: Executable program/skill: the injected/usable item is a parameterized FastMCP-compatible executable MCP tool (code) with a standardized interface, accompanied by a natural-language description and use_case. Surface form for retrieval is text (description+use_case); surface form for use is callable code.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Procedural, reusable skill/tool abstracted from a successful trajectory: above raw trajectories (hard-coded values lifted to parameters, task-specific context removed), i.e., a generalized parameterized primitive (e.g., the case-study extract_pdf_measurement tool) rather than a raw demonstration, distilled strategy/guideline, or full workflow.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Quality gating + relevance thresholding: (1) MCPs are harvested ONLY from successful master-agent trajectories (success filter) before entering the box; (2) abstraction removes instance-specific context to reduce brittle/overfit tools; (3) threshold-based RAG selection (tau=0.7) excludes low-similarity (likely irrelevant) MCPs at inference, with the ablation showing too-low tau injects irrelevant tools and too-high tau drops useful ones. Behavior analysis reports near-zero Right->Wrong regressions (1/1/0 across 1/2/3 generations), evidence the added tools rarely harm previously-correct answers. No retriever-aware training or explicit distractor-aware SFT.
memory_type: skill-library / procedural tool memory: the MCP Box is a curated library of reusable abstracted MCP tools (executable procedural skills). Not episodic-trajectory memory, graph memory, or latent memory.
write_back: Yes (during construction/self-evolution): MCPs synthesized from successful trajectories are abstracted and written into the MCP Box. However, write-back occurs in the offline construction loop, not during test-time deployment; the box is frozen at inference.
online_growth: No at deployment: the MCP Box is frozen during inference (no test-time growth). It grows only across the offline construction iterations k=1..K (e.g., #MCPs grows 26->46->74->102->128 from k=1 to k=5 on GAIA). So growth is offline/induced, not online/streaming.
write_back_trigger: On-success only, gated by task-label verification: an MCP is retained into the raw pool L only if it was generated during an execution where the master agent's answer matched the gold label (pi_master^(k)(x_i)=y_i). Failed trajectories contribute no MCPs. Retained MCPs are then abstracted into the box. There is no per-step, reflective-after-critique, or human-validated write trigger beyond the success filter.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only: only MCPs from SUCCESSFUL trajectories are stored and later retrieved; failed/negative experiences are discarded and not stored as contrastive negatives or corrective rules. (Contrast with experience-replay methods that store failures, e.g., Reflexion/ExpeL, which the paper cites as related but distinct.)
memory_evolution_update: Append-only across iterations (no merge/dedup/overwrite of stored entries): later generation rounds ADD newly harvested abstracted MCPs to the accumulated box; the paper explicitly states it preserves diversity and does NOT cluster/dedup ('Unlike traditional clustering approaches, our method preserves the diversity of MCP implementations'). Redundancy thus accumulates (effective-coverage ratio #Clusters/#MCPs drops from 1.00 at k=1 to 0.51 at k=5), and existing MCPs are not mutated or pruned.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/MCP selection is a fixed cosine-similarity threshold (or top-k) over frozen pre-trained embeddings; it is not an RL- or value-optimized retrieval policy (no soft Q-learning / M-MDP / learned router).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Partial/within-framework: the MCP Box is generated by a 'master' generalist agent and then transferred to a separately-instantiated 'specialized' agent (a form of capability transfer from generalist to specialist within the same Alita-based framework), and MCP is a standardized protocol enabling reuse across MCP-compatible agents. The paper contrasts itself with AgentDistill (which shares MCP boxes from strong teacher to weaker student across agents); Alita-G focuses on end-to-end self-specialization of one framework rather than cross-heterogeneous-framework collective memory. No multi-agent shared/collective memory pool.
benchmarks: GAIA (General AI Assistant; full validation set, 466 questions across Levels 1/2/3 -- note the paper cites 466 for the benchmark and uses the complete validation set, which is 165 questions in standard GAIA-val; [uncertain on exact count used]), PathVQA (medical pathology visual QA; 100 randomly sampled examples), and Humanity's Last Exam (HLE; 100 sampled examples).
benchmark_family: Tool-use / deep-research general-assistant (GAIA), multimodal medical visual QA (PathVQA), and frontier multi-disciplinary reasoning (HLE). GAIA is the headline tool/web-agent benchmark family; PathVQA and HLE are domain-specialization stress tests.
baselines: Octotools (tool-augmented agent framework, predefined tool collection); ODR-smolagents (Open Deep Research within HuggingFace Smolagents, strong general-purpose agent baseline); and the 'Original Agent System' = the master/base Alita-style agent (Manager Agent on Claude-Sonnet-4 + Web Agent on GPT-4.1) WITHOUT the specialized MCP Box, reported at both pass@1 and pass@3. Alita-G is also compared against its own variants Alita-G(1x) vs Alita-G(3x) (single vs triple-execution MCP boxes).
key_metrics: Accuracy (%) per GAIA difficulty level and total, and on PathVQA / HLE; reported at pass@1 and pass@3. Computational efficiency measured by average number of tokens consumed per example. Analysis also reports #MCPs, #clusters (connected components at sim>=0.7), mean/median pairwise MCP similarity, Wrong->Right and Right->Wrong flip counts, and average MCP calls per question.
headline_result: On GAIA validation, Alita-G (3x) achieves 83.03% pass@1 and 89.09% pass@3 (claimed new state-of-the-art), vs the Original Agent System's 75.15% pass@1 / 87.27% pass@3, while reducing mean tokens per example by ~15% (10,394 vs 12,305 avg tokens on GAIA). Relative gains: +50.5% relative over ODR-smolagents (55.15%) and +10.3% relative over the base agent at pass@1.
ablations: (1) RAG content components (Table 2, GAIA, 3x box): description+use_case 83.03% > description-only 81.82% > use_case-only 77.57% -- descriptions are the more generalizable retrieval signal. (2) MCP Box scalability (Table 4, GAIA): average accuracy 80.00 (k=1) -> 81.82 (k=2) -> 83.03 (k=3) -> 83.03 (k=4) -> 83.63 (k=5); #MCPs 26->46->74->102->128, #clusters 26->41->52->60->65, effective-coverage ratio drops 1.00->0.51, confirming diminishing returns with k=3 the cost/utility sweet spot. (3) Selection strategy/threshold (Table 3, 25-question GAIA subset): threshold tau sweep 0.65->0.90 peaks at tau=0.70 (84.0%); top-k sweep peaks at k=2-3 (80.0%); threshold-based generally beats fixed top-k. (4) Embedding encoder (Table 5, 25 questions): text-embedding-3-large 84.0% > text-embedding-3-small 80.0% > Qwen3-Embedding-8B 76.0% > NV-Embed-v2 72.0% = BGE-M3 72.0%. (5) MCP behavior (Table 6): overall acc 80.00/81.52/83.03 for 1/2/3 generations; Wrong->Right flips 9/12/13, Right->Wrong 1/1/0; avg MCP calls/question 1.9/2.2/2.4 and 2.7/3.0/3.4 on improved questions.
evaluation_decoupling: No intrinsic retrieval metrics decoupling: the paper does NOT report Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval completeness separately. Retrieval quality is assessed only indirectly via end-to-end task accuracy (RAG-content ablation, embedding-encoder ablation, threshold/top-k ablation) and via box-statistics proxies (#clusters, similarity), not via gold tool-relevance labels.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (task accuracy and token cost). Some process-level diagnostics are added: average MCP calls per question (and specifically on 'improved' questions), and Wrong->Right vs Right->Wrong flip counts, which probe whether tool use is targeted and non-regressive. No formal reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Explicit accuracy-with-lower-cost claim: Alita-G(3x) raises GAIA accuracy while cutting average tokens by ~15.5% (10,394 vs 12,305) relative to the base agent, attributed to the focused MCP toolset eliminating extensive tool-search; token reductions also hold on PathVQA (10,574 vs 12,542) and HLE (11,956 vs 14,730). Construction cost scales with iterations k (running the full task suite k times); k=3 is recommended as the cost/utility balance. Avg MCP calls per question 1.9-2.4. No wall-clock latency numbers reported [uncertain].
context_budget_and_selection_count: Adaptive / precision-driven by default: threshold mode (tau=0.7) yields a variable-size MCP subset adapted to task complexity (the paper argues this beats fixed top-k); a top-k mode (k in {1,2,3,5,10,20}) is available for predictable resource use. Selection narrows the toolset to reduce prompt bloat and tokens (~15% savings). No explicit fixed token budget cap is stated; the budget is controlled implicitly via the similarity threshold and the separation of lightweight index from on-demand code.
builds_on: Alita (Qiu et al., 2025, arXiv:2505.20286) -- the generalist agent with Manager+Web agents and MCP self-generation that Alita-G uses as its master/base architecture (Alita base = 75.15% pass@1 / 87.27% pass@3 on GAIA, matching Alita-G's 'Original' baseline). AgentDistill (Qiu et al., 2025, arXiv:2506.14728) -- training-free MCP-box distillation, whose MCP-abstraction principles Alita-G adopts (parameter generalization, context removal, interface standardization). Model Context Protocol / FastMCP (Anthropic 2024; Lowin 2024) for tool standardization. RAG-MCP (Gan & Sun, 2025, arXiv:2505.03275) for retrieval-augmented MCP/tool selection to mitigate prompt bloat. text-embedding-3-large (OpenAI 2024) for retrieval.
contrasts_with: Prior self-evolving agents that only do prompt rewriting or failure-retry (Reflexion, ExpeL, SAGE, Agent-Pro, Godel Agent, SELF, RAGEN, EvolveSearch) -- Alita-G instead accumulates and reuses executable tools (capability expansion vs knowledge/reasoning refinement). Auto-agent-generation works (AutoAgents, AutoGenesisAgent, EvoAgent, MetaGPT, AutoAgent, AFlow, AgentSquare, CAMEL, OpenHands) -- Alita-G generates complete deployable task-specific agents rather than isolated components/workflows. AgentDistill -- shares MCP boxes from strong teacher to weaker student, whereas Alita-G targets end-to-end self-specialization of a powerful generalist into a domain expert. Tool-use baselines Octotools (predefined tools) and ODR-smolagents.
lineage: Group E (tool-use): MCP-tool synthesis + retrieval-augmented tool selection lineage. Sits in the 2024-2025 tool-retrieval / self-evolving-tool-memory line: generalist MCP agent (Alita) -> training-free MCP-box distillation (AgentDistill) -> self-evolving generation of domain-specialist agents via abstracted MCP boxes with MCP-level RAG (Alita-G). Distinct from static API-retrieval tool-use (ToolLLM/Gorilla/ToolBench) by using agent-self-induced, abstracted, retrievable MCP tools.
